name: VirusTotal Community
summary: VirusTotal v3 reports (IP, domain, URL, file) and pivots (passive DNS, subdomains), limited to what a free community API key can read. Needs the analyst's own VirusTotal API key; a community key allows 240 requests/hour and 500/day. Desktop only.
description:
Enrichment and pivots from the VirusTotal v3 API, scoped to what a free community API key can read. Four report plugins write VirusTotal's verdict onto the IP Address, Domain, URL or File Hash they run on and add the infrastructure the report names; two fan-out plugins add passive DNS resolutions and subdomains. Endpoints a community key is refused are left out of the pack rather than tried and skipped. A paid key works unchanged; it only reaches more than this pack asks for.

## Plugins

### VT IP Report

- **Runs on:** IP Address.
- **Writes** the verdict block (below), plus `country_code`, `asn` and `organization`.
- **Adds** the certificate VirusTotal last saw on the IP's HTTPS port as a TLS Certificate (`presents certificate`, with `san_count`), and the names it lists as Domains (`names domain`) when it lists 25 or fewer.
- **Links, only when they already exist in the project:** the Autonomous System (`announced by`), the Netblock (`within netblock`) and that netblock's WHOIS Record (`has whois`). These are context the report mentions, so they are enriched but never created.

### VT Domain Report

- **Runs on:** Domain.
- **Writes** the verdict block with `vt_categories`, plus `registrar`, `created_date` and `expiration_date`.
- **Adds** up to 25 DNS Records VirusTotal last resolved (`has record`) and the last HTTPS certificate (`has certificate`, with `san_count`). The certificate's other names become Domains (`names domain`) only when it covers the domain (the name itself, or a wildcard one label up) and lists 25 names or fewer; a certificate that does not cover it is a hoster's default or a mismatch.
- **Fills and links** a WHOIS Record (`has whois`) only if one already exists.

### VT URL Report

- **Runs on:** URL.
- **Writes** the verdict block with `vt_categories` and `vt_threat_names`, plus `http_status`, `page_title`, `final_url` and `domain`.
- **Adds** the last serving IP Address (`resolves to`), up to 25 URLs of the redirect chain (`redirects to`), up to 25 hosts of the page's outgoing links as Domains (`has domain`), and the served content's SHA-256 as a File Hash (`has hash`).
- The redirect chain and outgoing links come from the URL report itself. The `redirects_to` and `contacted_domains` relationships answer 403 on a community key and are not called.

### VT File Report

- **Runs on:** File Hash or Malware nodes, and SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5 hashes typed into the Run dialog's **Hashes** field (separated by commas, spaces or new lines).
- **Writes** onto the File Hash: all three hashes, size, file type, tags, detection counts, the engines that flagged it with the malware names they gave, reputation, ssdeep and TLSH, and submission stats.
- A selected File Hash is enriched in place, even if it only held an MD5. Otherwise an existing one is matched by SHA-256, then SHA-1, then MD5, and only then is a new one created; the other selected nodes link to it (`has hash`).
- **Adds** VirusTotal's suggested threat label as a Malware family node (`classified as`). Its `malware_type` is the most-agreed VirusTotal category that the type's vocabulary has, otherwise `other`.

### VT Passive DNS

- **Runs on:** IP Address or Domain.
- **Adds** up to 120 resolutions per node: the hostnames seen on an IP as Domains, and the IPs a domain resolved to as IP Addresses, each with the detection counts the resolution carries for it, linked Domain `resolves to` IP Address.
- When VirusTotal holds more than 120, the run log says so.

### VT Subdomains

- **Runs on:** Domain.
- **Adds** up to 120 subdomains per domain as Domains linked `subdomain of`, each filled from the full report VirusTotal returns with it (verdict block, registrar, dates, categories) at no extra request.

## The verdict block

A full report is far too large to store (an IP report is about 40 KB of engine rows and RDAP), so each report plugin keeps a selection on the node it ran on:

| Property | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `vt_malicious`, `vt_suspicious`, `vt_harmless`, `vt_undetected` | detection counts from the last analysis |
| `vt_detections` | the engines that flagged it, by name and verdict; engines that said clean or unrated are dropped |
| `vt_reputation`, `vt_votes` | VirusTotal's community score and votes |
| `vt_categories` | the distinct vendor content categories (domain, URL) |
| `vt_tags`, `vt_analyzed` | VirusTotal's own tags, and when it last analysed the object |

These `vt_` properties are not declared by the type packs: they record one vendor's opinion at one moment, not the entity itself. The property panel still shows them. JARM is not kept, because it fingerprints a TLS listener on one port rather than the address or name it would be stored on. A run that finds anything flagged says so in its summary and logs which engines flagged it.

## Requirements

- **The analyst's own VirusTotal API key.** A free community key is enough. It is stored as a secret plugin setting and sent only in the `x-apikey` header, never in a URL.
- **Desktop app only.** VirusTotal sends no CORS headers, so a browser cannot read its replies; on the web the plugins refuse up front with that reason.
- Uses types from the Infrastructure and Threat type packs.

## Cost and limits

- A community key's allowance is 240 requests an hour, 500 a day and 15,500 a month, as VirusTotal reports it for the key (`GET /users/{key}`).
- One request per IP, domain or file looked up, and two per URL (its report and its last serving IP). Passive DNS and subdomains read 40 entries per request, so up to three requests per node.
- HTTP 429 is retried three times, after 15, 30 and 60 seconds (or the `Retry-After` the server sends, capped at 60 seconds). After that the run stops and says the allowance is hourly, so waiting within the run will not help.
- A rejected key (HTTP 401) ends the run. Per item, a 404 (no record), a 400 (malformed value) or a 403 (this key may not read it) is logged and skipped.

## What it contacts

- Only `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3`, with GET requests. VirusTotal sees every IP, domain, URL and hash looked up, under the analyst's key.
- **Passive.** Nothing is submitted for scanning, and the hosts under investigation are never contacted. A URL or file VirusTotal has no report on is skipped.
- Graph writes are staged: nothing reaches the project until the analyst reviews and applies them.

## Data and licences

Everything the pack adds is VirusTotal's data, read with the analyst's own key. The pack bundles no data of its own.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-virustotal-community (Apache-2.0). `dist/pack.mjs` is built from `src/virustotal-community.ts` with `node build.mjs`.

plugins.name: VT IP Report
plugins.description: Looks up each selected IP Address on VirusTotal and writes the verdict onto it: malicious/suspicious/harmless/undetected counts, the flagging engines (vt_detections), reputation, votes and tags, plus country_code, asn and organization. Creates the last HTTPS Certificate it presented ('presents certificate', with san_count) and, when the certificate lists 25 names or fewer, each as a Domain ('names domain'). Links an Autonomous System ('announced by'), Netblock ('within netblock') and that netblock's WHOIS Record ('has whois') only when they already exist in the project. Needs a VirusTotal API key. Desktop only.

Fills and links a WHOIS Record only if one already exists ('has whois'). Needs a VirusTotal API key. Desktop only.

Needs a VirusTotal API key. Desktop only.
